title: Glossy Dark Chocolate Ganache
summary: A versatile, glossy dark chocolate ganache that pours warm as a glaze and cools to a silky spreading or piping consistency.

ingredients.note: check the label; many contain soya lecithin or traces of milk

steps.title: Chop the chocolate
steps.text: Chop the chocolate finely and put it in the heatproof bowl. Small, even pieces melt quickly in the hot cream, so nothing needs to go back on the heat.

steps.title: Heat the cream
steps.text: Warm the cream and butter in the saucepan until bubbles break around the edge and the butter has melted, about 85-90 °C. Take it off before it boils hard.

steps.title: Stir to a gloss
steps.text: Pour the hot cream over the chocolate and leave it for 3 min. Stir gently from the centre, gradually widening the circles, until the ganache is smooth and glossy, then stir in the vanilla.

steps.title: Cool to use
steps.text: Pour it over a cake straight away while warm and fluid. To spread or pipe, leave it at room temperature for about 1 h, stirring occasionally, until it has the body of soft icing.

tips: The most common mistake is whisking hard, which beats in air bubbles; stir slowly with a spatula for a mirror-like finish.
If the ganache looks oily or grainy, whisk in 1-2 tbsp warm milk until it comes back together.
If it sets too firm, warm it over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring, until it softens.
Pour over a cake set on a rack so the excess runs off evenly.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 1 week. Warm gently over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring, until spreadable or pourable again.
